messages.author: db838ec007849ab9
messages.subject: trouble installing version 2.5 of rstan
parts:
Hello:
 
1. First, thank you for developing stan --- it's making a big difference in my work.
 
2. I'm upgrading from version 2.3 to version 2.5, using the instructions "RStan Getting Started". The installation goes well until I get the following
 
Attaching package: ‘Rcpp’

The following object is masked from ‘package:inline’:

    registerPlugin

cygwin warning:
  MS-DOS style path detected: C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-30~1.2/etc/x64/Makeconf
  Preferred POSIX equivalent is: /cygdrive/c/PROGRA~1/R/R-30~1.2/etc/x64/Makeconf
  CYGWIN environment variable option "nodosfilewarning" turns off this warning.
  Consult the user's guide for more details about POSIX paths:
    http://cygwin.com/cygwin-ug-net/using.html#using-pathnames
Warning in install.packages :
  InternetOpenUrl failed: 'The operation timed out'
Warning in install.packages :
  InternetOpenUrl failed: 'The operation timed out'
Warning in install.packages :
  unable to access index for repository http://rstan.org/repo/bin/windows/contrib/3.0
Installing package into ‘C:/Users/ellefsen/Documents/R/win-library/3.0’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
Warning in install.packages :
  InternetOpenUrl failed: 'The operation timed out'
Warning in install.packages :
  InternetOpenUrl failed: 'The operation timed out'
Warning in install.packages :
  unable to access index for repository http://rstan.org/repo/src/contrib
Warning in install.packages :
  package ‘rstan’ is not available (for R version 3.0.2)

 Show Traceback
 
 Rerun with Debug
 
Error in library(rstan) : there is no package called ‘rstan’
 
In addition: Warning message:
package ‘inline’ was built under R version 3.0.3 
 
If I understand correctly, the problem is with the following code from function "install_rstan":
options(repos = c(getOption("repos"), rstan = "http://rstan.org/repo/"))
install.packages("rstan", type = 'source')
That is, function install.packages is unable to find http://rstan.org/repo/. As requested, here is the session info:
 
R version 3.0.2 (2013-09-25)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252  LC_CTYPE=English_United States.1252   
[3] LC_MONETARY=English_United States.1252 LC_NUMERIC=C                          
[5] LC_TIME=English_United States.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] Rcpp_0.11.3   inline_0.3.13

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_3.0.2
3. Thank you for your help.
 
Karl Ellefsen

messages.subject: Re: trouble installing version 2.5 of rstan
parts:
Maybe a change in policy with your firewall? If you can download
http://rstan.org/repo/src/contrib/rstan_2.5.0.tar.gz
with a web browser, you can then install rstan via R CMD INSTALL rstan_2.5.0.tar.gz

parts:
During lunchtime I went to the public library, because the library network is separate from my work network. I was able to download the tar file http://rstan.org/repo/src/contrib/rstan_2.5.0.tar.gz, but http://rstan.org and http://srtan.org/repo gave me the forbidden message (403?). These results are consistent with Bob Carpenter's results.
 
Now that I'm back at work, I tested http://rstan.org/repo/src/contrib/rstan_2.5.0.tar.gz and http://rstan.org/repo again. Both times I get "This page can't be displayed," which, I guess, is equivalent to the 403 message.

Karl Ellefsen
